message.content:
**Pet‑friendly train station in Miami** | Station | Operator | Pet Policy Highlights | |---------|----------|-----------------------| | **Miami Central Station** (also known as *Miami Amtrak Station*) | Amtrak (Silver Service – Silver Meteor & Silver Star) | • Pets are allowed on Amtrak’s Silver Service trains when traveling between New York City and Miami.
• Pets must be in a carrier that fits under the seat or in the luggage area.
• A small fee (usually $5–$10 per pet) applies.
• The station itself has no dedicated “pet lounge,” but the trains’ onboard facilities (e.g., restrooms, seating) are accessible for pets. | ### How to travel with a pet from Miami Central Station 1. **Book Early** – Reserve a pet spot on the train when you purchase your ticket. Amtrak’s online booking system or customer service can confirm availability. 2. **Prepare Your Pet** – Use a sturdy carrier that meets Amtrak’s size limits (under 18 inches tall, 12 inches wide, 12 inches deep). Bring water, a leash, and any necessary medication. 3. **Arrive Early** – Get to the station at least 30 minutes before departure to allow time for check‑in and boarding with your pet. 4. **Follow Onboard Rules** – Keep your pet in its carrier during the entire journey, except when using the restroom (if the train has a dedicated pet area or you’re allowed to bring your pet out briefly). ### Why this is the best option - **Miami Central Station** is the only major passenger rail hub in Miami, serving Amtrak’s long‑distance routes. - Amtrak’s pet policy is clear and widely used, making it easier to plan and avoid surprises. - While the station itself doesn’t have a dedicated pet lounge, the trains’ onboard facilities are designed to accommodate pets safely. If you’re looking for a different type of pet‑friendly transit (e.g., buses, rideshares), let me know and I can help find those options too!
